title: A Connectivity-Order Law and Conditional Minimal-Mechanism Identification in Many-Body Geometric Phases
authors: Kuo Hai, Junhao Huang, Qiong Chen, Wenhua Hai
abstract: The value of a multiqubit geometric phase at a single operating point does not reveal whether it was generated directly or through a connected sequence of lower-body interactions. For analytic, gapped, nondegenerate Abelian holonomies, we jointly resolve logical support and independently calibrated coupling support. Every nonzero connected response must involve an active set that connects and covers the target and must contain one factor of each active coupling, yielding the sharp onset bound $ν_S \geq τ_E(S)$. The same selection law applies locally to projected Berry curvature. Conversely, an unrestricted finite-dimensional construction realizes all responses allowed by the connected-cover condition simultaneously, making the condition necessary and sufficient within this theorem class. Operationally, simultaneous confidence bands certify detected mixed responses while controlling false positives; a factor-of-two separation condition additionally recovers exact library-relative response minima. In a complete dictionary, nontriviality of every minimal-cover response is generically necessary and sufficient for these minima to coincide with the minimal calibrated mechanisms. Three-qubit Wilson calculations distinguish direct and pair-mediated routes with the same endpoint phase, and a synthetic Ramsey audit locates the finite-resolution boundary.
summary: This theoretical work develops a 'connectivity-order law' to solve the problem of identifying the physical mechanism responsible for a measured many-body geometric phase. By employing advanced algebraic and combinatorial methods, the authors prove that the phase value constrains the underlying interactions to those that form a connected cover. This provides a powerful diagnostic tool for characterizing quantum system dynamics.
main_problem: The core problem is determining the generating mechanism (direct vs. connected sequence of lower-body interactions) of a measured many-body geometric phase ($\Phi_S$) from its value alone.
main_result:
The paper establishes a 'connectivity-order law' stating that a nonzero connected response must involve an active set that connects and covers the target support, leading to the bound $

method: The authors use advanced mathematical tools including Möbius inversion on subset lattices, joint-support projectors, and developing a 'minimal-cover order law' to analyze the structure of Abelian holonomies.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on multiqubit systems exhibiting Abelian holonomies, derived from Hamiltonians structured with coupling terms, applicable to settings like two-spin NMR or semiconductor spin-qubits.
key_observables: The multiqubit geometric phase ($\Phi_S$), locally irreducible phase ($\Phi_S$), and confidence bands for detecting mixed responses.
important_parameters: The analysis is restricted to analytic, gapped, nondegenerate Abelian holonomies; the separation condition $|\Phi_S| > 2\Delta$ is key for identifying exact minima.
main_assumptions: The results are derived under the assumption of analytic, gapped, and nondegenerate Abelian holonomies, and the method cannot resolve uncalibrated virtual paths.

paper_structure: The paper builds from identifying the mechanism-identifiability problem, developing the connectivity-order law via joint support projectors, and concluding with necessary and sufficient conditions for minimal-cover response identification.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous mathematical tools to distinguish the physical origin of quantum phase accumulation, which is crucial for designing robust quantum gates and characterizing quantum hardware.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Physical logic of the connectivity-order law. a, Removing global and subsystem- local phases leaves the irreducible many-body phase. b, Factorized blocks contribute additively. c, Joint logical–coupling resolution permits exactly connected covers at the theorem-class level; the local curvature obeys the same rule. d, The minimum cover fixes the earliest theorem-class- allowed onset. Simultaneous bands certify detected responses, beta-min yields exact response minima, and only a complete identifiable family turns those minima into calibrated mechanisms generically. The sharpness construction is not a hardware design.

Figure 3: Two-stage acquisition and three-layer inference for connected-phase mech- anism tests. A radial onset gives one-sided architecture and locality exclusions. Simultaneous mixed-response bands then certify genuine connected-cover responses in a prespecified cali- brated library. Beta-min gives exact library-relative minima, while completeness plus family identifiability is additionally required for generic minimal-mechanism interpretation.
